sentences.text: Challenging the adequacy of compensation awarded to them, the claimants in LAC No.80/2008 on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Mangaluru have preferred this appeal.

2. Under the preliminary notification dated 30.08.2007 the Deputy Commissioner, D.K.District proposed for acquisition of 0.15 acres of land in Sy.No.52/3 of Jeppinamogaru village for the purpose of Underground Drainage construction for Mangaluru City by the Mangaluru Municipal Corporation in collaboration with Area Development Board.
Out of the said 0.15 cents 14 cents of land belonged to the claimants.
On final notification, the Special Land Acquisition Officer passed final award dated 21.07.2008 granting compensation of Rs.31,000/- per cent.
3. On the application of the appellants the Land Acquisition Officer referred the matter to Prl.
Senior Civil Judge, Mangaluru under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act
for determination of the compensation payable
. The appellants contended that the market value of the acquired land is not less than Rs.2,00,000/- per cent as that comes under the Mangaluru Municipal Corporation limits.
They further contended that the lands are fertile lands having road on both side.
They claimed that they have 27 coconut yielding trees and 1 Indian fig/athi tree with a well in the acquired land.
4. Before the Reference Court, claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and on their behalf Exs.P1 to P3 were marked.
Respondent did not lead any evidence.
5. The Reference Court on hearing the parties by the impugned order granted compensation at the rate of Rs.33,800/- per cent with statutory benefits.
The market value of the buildings and trees estimated and determined at the rate of Rs.18,198/- and Rs.1,79,329/- by the Land Acquisition Officer was maintained.

6. Before the Reference Court the appellants produced Ex.P1 the Engineer's valuation with sketch dated 30.05.2008, Ex.P2 certified copy of the market valuation of sites as on 18.04.2011 and Ex.P3 the certified copy of gazette notification regarding market value/Sub-Registrar Guidance value of the land in Jeppinamogaru village.
Under Ex.P1 the private engineer has estimated the value of the acquired land at 1,50,000/- per cent, Well and the trees at Rs.1,29,000/-.
The total value was estimated at Rs.22,29,000/-.
As per Ex.P2 as on 18.04.2011 it was said that value of the residential sites within that village limits was Rs.75,000/- to 1,55,000/- per cent.
As per Ex.P3 the notification regarding SR value of the land, the value of the lands situated within the limits of Jeppinamogaru village was Rs.40,000/- to 1,10,000/- per cent.
7. The Reference Court declined to accept Ex.P1 as that was valuation made by a private person and the author of Ex.P1 was not examined.
Therefore, the Reference Court was justified in rejecting that.

sentences.text: So far as Ex.P2 the reference Court held that the market value has to be determined on the basis of sales statistics for a period of three years preceding the notification, Ex.P2 is the market value of the property determined under the notification dated 12.04.2011.
Since Ex.P2 was a sale deed subsequent to the notification, reference Court justifiably rejected the same as basis of the market value.
8. On exclusion of Exs.P1 and P2, before the Reference Court except Ex.P3 there was no other material for determination of the market value.

The Reference Court says that the market value of the acquired land has to be estimated on the basis of the sales statistics for a period of three years preceding the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, the Land acquisition Officer determined the market value at Rs.31,000/- per cent based on the sale deeds dated 05.10.2004 and 08.07.2005 and 04.06.2006 in respect of punja lands/barren lands and sale deed dated 02.08.2006 in respect of land converted for non- agricultural purpose.
The Reference Court referring to the sale deeds of the year 2004, 2005 and 2006 relied on by the Land Acquisition officer in the award determined the market value at Rs.33,790/- per cent.

9. The market value of the land has to be determined as prescribed under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act which reads as follows:
"23. Matters to be considered on determining compensation.

sentences.text:
The above provisions show that in determining the amount of compensation the Court has to take into consideration the market value of the land as on the date of publication of the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act and the loss suffered by the land owner due to taking of standing trees or crops, wells etc.
10. Section 23(1)(A) of the Act states that to the market value of the land as on the date of 4(1)
notification, the market value of 12% has to be added from the date of preliminary notification or from the date of taking possession of the land whichever is earlier.
Section 23 does not say that the Court shall rely only on the sales statistics.
All sales of immovable properties will be generally registered in the office of the Sub-Registrar.
Therefore the notification issued by the Government regarding the market value of the land during the said period can be relied.

11. The Division Bench of this Court in K.Gopala Gowda vs. Special Land Acquisition Officer1 while considering the beneficial value of the notification issued by the Government regarding Sub-Registrar's value held as follows:
"18.

sentences.text: The Government of Karnataka, in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 68 read with Section 45B of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act No. 34 of 1957)

entities.text: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957 (Karnataka Act No. 34 of 1957)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: , has framed the rules called the Karnataka Stamp (Constitution of Committee for Estimation of Property) Rules, 1992.

entities.text: Karnataka Stamp (Constitution of Committee for Estimation of Property) Rules, 1992
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Rule 3 of the said Rules deals with constitution of the Committee, whereas Rule 4 thereof deals with the manner of estimating the market value of properties.

The Committee is required to determine the market value of the property taking into account several factors mentioned in Clauses (a) to (d) with regard to KCCR 2004 1 333 the lands, house-suites and buildings, respectively.
Therefore, undoubtedly, the estimation of the market value vide Exhibit-P. 16 by the Government of Karnataka has statutory basis.

At the same time, it needs to be noticed that simply because Exhibit-P. 16 has a statutory basis, it cannot be said that the Civil Court has to determine the actual market value of the acquired land, whether under the Land Acquisition Act or Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, in terms of the value determined by the Government in its Notification issued under the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957.
It is trite that compensation of the acquired land has to be determined in terms of Provisions of Sections 23 and 24 of the Act.
Sections 23 and 24 of the Act deal with what are relevant and what are irrelevant considerations while determining the actual market value of the acquired land.

At the same time, it also needs to be noticed that Exhibit-P.16 undoubtedly could be a piece of relevant evidence along with other pieces of relevant evidence for decision-making for the Civil Court while determining the actual market value of the acquired land as on the date of Section 4(1) Notification or under Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act."
(Emphasis supplied)
12. Reading of the above paragraph shows that the notification issued by the Government of Karnataka regarding the market value of the property has a statutory basis.

In para 19 of the same Victor Simon D Souza vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 8 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94391487/
4 judgment, it was held that in the absence of comparable sale deeds, such notification can be relied on in determining the market value.

sentences.text: It is settled position of law that apart from the sale statistics the Land Acquisition Officer and the Reference Court have to take into consideration the advantages of the land.
As per respondents this land was acquired for the purpose of laying the UGD within the limits of Mangaluru City Corporation.
That itself goes to show that the land was in urban area.
13. Though the land was not converted for nonagricultural purpose, the same had the advantages of urban land/non agricultural land.
Under the said circumstance the Reference Court was not justified in rejecting Ex.P3 as basis for determining the market value of the land.
The impugned award needs to be modified.

14. Learned counsel for the appellant though contended that the land had the benefit of commercial purpose, in the evidence of PW.1 nothing was elicited to show that there were any commercial buildings or commercial activities being taken place in the surrounding lands.
Therefore though the land has the benefit of urban land, the contention that it had the potentiality of being used for commercial purpose cannot be accepted.
As per Ex.P3 the highest market value fixed for nonagricultural lands used for residential purpose was Rs.60,000/- per cent.
Therefore, the claimants who were in the locality of Adimaya Devasthana were entitled to Rs.60,000/- per cent.
Rs.1,10,000/- per cent notified in Ex.P3 was with reference to properties in Gurunagar cross, Adam Kudru road, Jeppinamogaru B village and Adimaya temple road.
The appellants' own document Ex.P1 does not indicate that the land in question situated either in Gurunagar cross or B village or on Adam Kudru road.
Therefore, the market value of the land at Rs.60,000/- per cent shown in Ex.P3 relating to land situated in Adimaya Temple Road has to be taken.
It is just to award compensation at Rs.60,000/- per cent.
The award of the Reference Court needs to modified accordingly.

Hence the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed.
ii) The impugned award is modified as follows:
a) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.60,000/- per cent for the acquired land with all statutory benefits.
- 11 - b) The award of the Land Acquisition Officer with regard to buildings and trees and other statutory benefits is maintained.
c) The rest of the award is maintained.
